title: How To Simplify Classroom Management
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Reacting against the clutter of clip charts, prize boxes, and incentive systems that dominate many classrooms, Linsin argues classroom management can be stripped down to a handful of core principles. He lists rules that cover every possible misbehavior, consistent enforcement of consequences, a genuine willingness to follow through, calm and quick interactions with misbehaving students, an interesting and enjoyable learning environment, rapport-building through humor and trust, a clean and peaceful classroom environment, and predictable consistency that makes the classroom 'make sense' to students. He describes these principles as working together regardless of school setting or student population, and positions ongoing site content as a way to deepen the knowledge needed to implement them effectively, rather than adding new complexity.
points: Classroom management can be reduced to a handful of guiding principles rather than a clutter of charts, prizes, and incentive systems.
Core principles include comprehensive rules, consistent consequence enforcement, and genuine willingness to follow through every time.
Calm, quick interactions with misbehaving students avoid the friction of anger, hurt feelings, or arguing.
An interesting, enjoyable learning environment and strong rapport 'cover up a multitude of classroom management mistakes.'
Predictable, consistent teacher behavior makes the classroom environment 'make sense' to students, which itself supports good behavior.
quotes: Clip charts, prize boxes, incentive systems, seating arrangements, stickers, pep-talks, noise makers, red cards, table points, trinkets, tokens, awards, erasers, free time, computer time, first in line, contracts, privileges, and… enough!!!
For many, classroom management has become too complicated. It doesn’t need to be. All you need are a few guiding principles.
You have to be willing to enforce a consequence every time a rule is broken. This is critical to effective classroom management. Most teachers don’t follow through consistently.
Creating a fun, stimulating learning environment covers up a multitude of classroom management mistakes. Kids who like school behave better—a lot better.
If your students like/love being in your classroom, they won’t want to be separated from it. This is what makes time-out work.
Your students must know what to expect every time they enter your classroom. Therefore, you must be consistently pleasant.
